rules: A continuity system protects a function, not an object.
Every active system has a named owner, a backup, a next review time, and a failure escalation.
Official hazard instructions and emergency routes override this catalog.
A household may leave a field blank only when it records who will resolve it and by when.

systems.label: Information
systems.question: What is confirmed, by whom, and when will it be checked again?
systems.protect: Use official warnings and one shared update channel.
systems.backup: Keep a battery radio, written contacts, and a scheduled briefing.
systems.failure_escalation: Instructions conflict, the warning source is unavailable, or nobody can receive updates.
systems.owner_prompt: Who verifies and posts the next update?

systems.label: Air and hazard
systems.question: Is the place safe to occupy?
systems.protect: Run the environmental override before troubleshooting or conserving supplies.
systems.backup: Leave by a safe route and report from outside.
systems.failure_escalation: Fire, smoke, CO alarm, gas, chemical exposure, electrical danger, symptoms, or uncertainty.
systems.owner_prompt: Who confirms the safe area and prevents re-entry?

systems.label: Care and power
systems.question: Which treatment, device, medicine, or caregiver function cannot pause?
systems.protect: Use the approved personal backup and call early while a safe bridge remains.
systems.backup: Move to a known staffed, powered, accessible destination.
systems.failure_escalation: A life-supporting function, critical dose, storage condition, or caregiver bridge cannot be maintained.
systems.owner_prompt: Who knows the remaining runtime and transfer route?

systems.label: Water
systems.question: What water is safe, how much remains, and what use has priority?
systems.protect: Separate drinking and food-preparation water from washing and waste water.
systems.backup: Use sealed stores or official distribution and follow local water notices.
systems.failure_escalation: No safe drinking source, contamination warning, or essential care requires more than the safe reserve.
systems.owner_prompt: Who records stock, use, source status, and the next refill?

systems.label: Temperature and shelter
systems.question: Can everyone remain dry, ventilated, and within a safe thermal environment?
systems.protect: Use the safest available shelter and reduce exposure before optimizing comfort.
systems.backup: Move early to a safer, cooler, warmer, or officially designated place.
systems.failure_escalation: Confusion, collapse, severe symptoms, unsafe structure, smoke, flooding, or inability to move a vulnerable person.
systems.owner_prompt: Who checks room conditions and people needing help?

systems.label: Food and cooking
systems.question: What can be eaten safely with the available water, energy, and access needs?
systems.protect: Use safe perishables first, keep cold storage closed, and preserve familiar usable foods.
systems.backup: Shift to shelf-stable food that requires little water or power.
systems.failure_escalation: Food safety is uncertain, a medically necessary intake cannot be maintained, or cooking introduces fire or CO risk.
systems.owner_prompt: Who tracks refrigeration status, allergies, and the next meal?

systems.label: Sanitation
systems.question: How are hands, toilets, waste, and clean zones kept separate?
systems.protect: Reserve safe water for drinking and essential food use; separate clean and dirty handling.
systems.backup: Use the household toilet-failure plan and current municipal instructions.
systems.failure_escalation: Waste contaminates living or food areas, handwashing fails, sewage enters the building, or local instructions require leaving.
systems.owner_prompt: Who owns toilet status, handwashing, waste route, and cleaning supplies?

systems.label: People, access, and transport
systems.question: Who cannot receive a warning, leave, enter, communicate, or reach the destination without help?
systems.protect: Ask what support is wanted and name the destination, transport, entry, and communication method.
systems.backup: Use a second route, second helper, or staffed public destination.
systems.failure_escalation: A person, child, animal, essential device, or caregiver cannot be moved or supported before the safe window ends.
systems.owner_prompt: Who checks people, animals, keys, documents, transport, and entry?

roles.label: Coordination
roles.owns: task board, owners, deadlines, next briefing
roles.backup: a named deputy can read the same log
roles.failure_mode: one confident person becomes the entire system

roles.label: Care
roles.owns: injury, medication, devices, children, dependants, animals
roles.backup: care contacts and transfer information are written down
roles.failure_mode: the calmest caregiver is assumed to need no relief

roles.label: Supplies
roles.owns: water, food, batteries, hygiene, stock and rate of use
roles.backup: another person can find and count the stock
roles.failure_mode: inventory lives in one person's memory

roles.label: Information
roles.owns: official sources, confirmed facts, uncertainty, update time
roles.backup: radio, written contacts, and a second verification route
roles.failure_mode: rumour and fact share the same channel

roles.label: Access and logistics
roles.owns: exits, transport, entry, mobility, communication, destination
roles.backup: a second route and helper are named
roles.failure_mode: the plan assumes every body, device, and door works

handoff_fields: people, dependants, animals, and essential care
system status: okay / limited / failed / unknown
